consensus_summary: Hell primarily denotes the final place or state of eternal conscious punishment, torment, and separation from God for the unrepentant wicked, expressed via fire/Gehenna imagery; common alternatives include annihilationism, universalism, present-existential readings, and the scholarly lexical distinction of Sheol/Hades vs. Gehenna/Tartarus.
book_summary: Hell is one English word laid over two different things: Sheol/Hades (the grave swallowing righteous and wicked alike) and Gehenna (the judgment that destroys); the doctrine changes with the underlying word.
consensus_core_identification: final place/state of eternal divine punishment and separation from God for the unrepentant wicked
book_core_identification: English term conflating two distinct biblical realities (Sheol/Hades as universal grave vs. Gehenna as destroying judgment)
boundary_disagreement: Book splits the traditional single referent so that Sheol/Hades passages cover all the dead without punitive finality while Gehenna covers only destroying judgment; consensus primary keeps a unified postmortem punitive destiny for the wicked under the one English term.
material_contradiction: Consensus core treats hell as one coherent final punitive destiny (eternal conscious torment/separation); book replaces that with two non-identical things under the English word, so the traditional unified hell is not a biblical identity and doctrines diverge by which term is meant.
rationale: Consensus primary core is the historically dominant eternal-punishment place/state. Book's core instead identifies the term itself as an overlay on two different realities (grave for all vs. judgment that destroys), a claim consensus lists only among alternatives. The cores cannot both hold of the same referent in the same sense: accepting the dual overlay requires rejecting or replacing the unified final-punishment identification. Book's 'destroys' further tilts Gehenna toward annihilationist alternatives, but the decisive divergence is the replaced single referent. Printed pair (Ps 16:10 Sheol + Matt 10:28 Gehenna) illustrates the split without alone proving the full doctrine-change claim.
strongest_objection: The lexical distinction is already a common alternative in the consensus responses, so the book may be elevating a known scholarly point rather than introducing a full replacement of the primary punitive referent; traditionalists routinely accept word distinctions while retaining eternal conscious punishment for Gehenna.
